count_semantics.warning: 'count' is ambiguous. summarize's r(N) counts observations with a NON-MISSING value of the variable; the -count- command counts observations that satisfy if/in regardless of missingness. They agree for mpg (no missing) but will not agree for rep78 (5 missing). dash kpi count() currently uses summarize r(N), i.e. the non-missing count.

percentile_definition.definition: Stata's percentile (summarize, detail; _pctile; pctile; tabstat p25/p50/p75; egen pctile) is the AVERAGED INVERSE EMPIRICAL CDF, Hyndman-Fan type 2. With the N non-missing values sorted x(1) <= ... <= x(N) and j = N*p/100: if j is an integer the answer is (x(j)+x(j+1))/2, otherwise it is x(ceil(j)). No interpolation between order statistics other than that midpoint. Weights change j to the running sum of weights, but dash passes no weights to its KPI code.

numpy_pandas_default_type7.note: numpy.percentile / pandas .quantile() / .median() default to linear interpolation (Hyndman-Fan type 7) and DISAGREE with Stata. dash_render.py and the CustomJS KPI code must reproduce the Stata rule, not the pandas one.

centile.note: -centile- uses a DIFFERENT, interpolating definition and is not the one summarize,detail uses. Never use centile to produce a dash KPI percentile.

variance_and_sd.rule: summarize r(Var) and r(sd) use the N-1 divisor (sample variance). pandas .var()/.std() default to ddof=1 and therefore agree; numpy .var()/.std() default to ddof=0 and do NOT.

skewness.rule: summarize, detail r(skewness) is the BIASED / population moment ratio m3 / m2^1.5, where m_k = (1/N)*sum((x-xbar)^k) with the N divisor - not the sample-corrected g1 that scipy.stats.skew(bias=False) or Excel's SKEW() return. scipy.stats.skew(x) with its default bias=True matches Stata.

iqr.rule: IQR is simply p75 - p25 under the same type-2 percentile rule; tabstat's iqr agrees exactly.

scale.setup: 200,000 observations, 200,000 distinct values; a long numeric x and a str12 s.
scale.note: tabulate and levelsof both FAIL at 200k distinct values (rc 134 and rc 198). egen group() answers correctly and is the fastest of the six. This is the deciding measurement.

verdict.current_dash_code: _dash_kpi: quietly codebook `kpi_var' `if' `in' ; local kpi_value = r(unique)  ->  kpi_value is always system missing '.'
verdict.recommended: tempvar g ; quietly egen `g' = group(`kpi_var') `if' `in' ; quietly summarize `g', meanonly ; local kpi_value = r(max)
verdict.why: Correct for numeric and string variables, excludes missing by default (matching pandas .nunique() and a JavaScript Set over non-null values), has no distinct-value ceiling, needs no macro to hold the levels, and was the fastest command measured at 200,000 distinct values.
verdict.edge_case_zero_rows: If the if/in selection is empty, or every value is missing, egen group() leaves the temp variable all-missing and summarize, meanonly sets r(max) to missing with r(N)==0. The implementation must special-case r(N)==0 and report a dcount of 0 rather than '.'.
verdict.runner_up: levelsof `var' `if' `in' -> r(r). Simpler, and correct on small data, but it also materialises r(levels) and dies with rc 198 once that macro exceeds c(macrolen) = 645,200 characters.
do_not_use: inspect (r(N_unique) is missing once there are 100 or more distinct values; numeric-only)

stata_rules.summary: Stata 14+ accepts Unicode letters in variable names. The rule measured here: the name must start with a Unicode LETTER or an underscore and may then contain Unicode letters, ASCII digits and underscores. Length is limited to 32 CHARACTERS, not 32 bytes.

length_limit.conclusion: The 32 limit is counted in characters (ustrlen), not bytes: a 32-character / 96-byte CJK name is accepted and a 33-character name is rejected with rc 198, exactly like ASCII.

surprises: An emoji is accepted INSIDE a name: generate x😀 = _n succeeded with rc 0. Stata treats the emoji as a name character once the name starts with a letter.
A full-width digit does not count as a digit for the leading-character rule: the name starting with U+FF17 was rejected with rc 198, like an ASCII leading digit.
Full-width Latin letters (U+FF33 ...) are accepted as letters.

one_real_wart_but_not_unicode.conclusion: Identical for ASCII and Unicode, so this is a missing-variable-label fallback bug, NOT a Unicode bug. Anyone who tested Unicode with an unlabelled variable would have mistaken it for one.

where_unicode_IS_rejected.message: dash kpi: syntax is stat(varname), e.g. mean(mpg).
where_unicode_IS_rejected.cause: _dash_kpi validates the whole stat(var) spec with regexm(`statspec', "^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)\(([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\)$"), an ASCII-only character class.
where_unicode_IS_rejected.severity: Loud, not silent - the user gets rc 198 and a message. But it is still wrong: Stata accepts the name and dash's own plotting path accepts it.
where_unicode_IS_rejected.fix: Match the variable part with ustrregexm and Stata's own name rule, or drop the regex for the variable and let -confirm variable- (already called on the next line) do the validating.

bugs_found.title: Every name() in dash is rejected on Stata 18+: the bounded regex quantifier {0,31} is not supported under version 16.0
bugs_found.symptom: dash scatter mpg weight, name(gasc)  ->  'dash: invalid graph name 'gasc''  rc 198.  dash kpi mean(mpg), title(t) name(kasc)  ->  'dash kpi: invalid name 'kasc''  rc 198.  Both the KPI subcommand and every named graph, and therefore dash build, are unusable.
bugs_found.root_cause: dash.ado validates names with regexm("`name'", "^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,31}$"). Stata 18 replaced the engine behind regexm(); the OLD engine, which is what -version 16.0- (declared at the top of every dash program) selects, does not support the {n,m} interval quantifier and treats {0,31} as literal text, so the pattern can never match.
bugs_found.fix: Use ustrregexm(), which honours {0,31} under every version setting, or express the length limit without an interval quantifier: regexm("`name'", "^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$") & ustrlen("`name'") <= 32.
bugs_found.regression_test: cscript: assert that dash scatter mpg weight, name(g1) returns rc 0 and that dash kpi mean(mpg), title(T) name(k1) returns rc 0 and registers $dash_kpi_k1_val.

bugs_found.title: dcount always evaluates to system missing because codebook returns nothing
bugs_found.symptom: dash kpi dcount(rep78), ... stores kpi_value = '.' rather than 5.
bugs_found.root_cause: _dash_kpi runs `quietly codebook `kpi_var'` and reads r(unique). codebook leaves no r(unique) - it leaves an entirely empty r() for a numeric variable, and only r(str_embedded)/r(str_type) for a string one.

bugs_found.fix: Replace with egen group() + summarize, meanonly as set out in dcount.verdict.recommended.
